title:
Space engineering
Space data links - Telemetry synchronization and channel coding
short_title: ECSS TM Synchronization and Channel Coding (2008)
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-50-01C Working Group)
status_notes: Second issue (31 July 2008), following ECSS-E-50-01A (first issue, 6 November 2007); ECSS-E-50-01B was never issued (change log, p. 3). The document does not state that it is superseded. The library's ECSS-E-AS-50-21C Rev. 2 (5 December 2024) states that ECSS-E-ST-50-01C is superseded by ECSS-E-AS-50-21 (latest version), the ECSS Adoption Notice of CCSDS 131.0-B-x (that notice, pp. 3 and 6).

contents.title: Terms specific to the present standard
Relationship of ASM to Reed-Solomon and turbo codeblocks
Transformation between Berlekamp and conventional representations (informative)

key_points.text: Category A spacecraft are those at an altitude above the Earth's surface of less than 2 × 10^6 km; category B at or above 2 × 10^6 km.
Bit numbering: the first transmitted bit of an N-bit field is bit 0 and is the most significant bit.

The basic convolutional code is rate 1/2, constraint length 7, with connection vectors G1 = 1111001 (171 octal) and G2 = 1011011 (133 octal) and symbol inversion on the G2 output path; the punctured versions (rates 2/3, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8) have no inversion.

Soft bit decisions with at least 3-bit quantization shall be used for the convolutional decoder; if NRZ-L to NRZ-M conversion is used it should be done at the encoder input and reversed at the decoder output.
Decoding failures of the Viterbi decoder are not signalled and produce error bursts, so ECSS-E-ST-50-03 requires a CRC on TM frames unless Reed-Solomon coding is used.
Reed-Solomon code: J = 8 bits per symbol, E = 16, n = 255, 32 parity symbols and k = 223 information symbols per codeword; field generator polynomial F(x) = x^8 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1.
The Reed-Solomon interleaving depth I shall be 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 8 (I=1 means no interleaving), and shall be fixed on a physical channel for a mission phase; maximum codeblock length is 255I symbols.
The E=8 (255,239) Reed-Solomon code shall only be used with 4D-8PSK-TCM modulation, shall not be concatenated with a convolutional code and shall use interleaving depth I=8.
Turbo information block lengths are 1784, 3568, 7136 and 8920 bits (223 × 1, 2, 4 and 5 octets), with codeblock lengths of 3576/7152 bits for 1784 at rates 1/2 and 1/4.
The ASM is 1ACFFC1D for non-turbo-coded data, 034776C7 272895B0 for rate-1/2 turbo and 034776C7 272895B0 FCB88938 D8D76A4F for rate-1/4 turbo coded data.
The ASM immediately precedes each codeblock or frame with no intervening bits, and is never presented to the Reed-Solomon or turbo encoder or decoder.
A recorded frame stream embedded in real-time frames shall use the embedded ASM 352EF853; it shall not be used with turbo-coded frames.
Presence or absence of pseudo-randomization is fixed for a physical channel and is not signalled in the telemetry: the receiver knows it a priori.
The pseudo-random sequence is generated by h(x) = x^8 + x^7 + x^5 + x^3 + 1, repeats after 255 bits, and is never exclusive-ORed with the ASM.
Maximum TM frame lengths with E=16 Reed-Solomon: 223, 446, 669, 892, 1115 and 1784 octets for I = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8; with E=8 and I=8, 1912 octets.

Compared with ESA-PSS-04-103 (1989), the standard adds punctured convolutional codes, RS E=8 restricted to 4D-8PSK-TCM and turbo codes, and drops the PSS restriction on using the randomizer with convolutional coding under BPSK.
The codes are a subset of CCSDS 131.0-B-1: the CCSDS recommendations also have turbo rates 1/3 and 1/6 and unrestricted E=8 Reed-Solomon codes.

Mission configuration parameters of a physical channel: channel coding scheme, frame length, pseudo-randomization, embedded-stream ASM use, convolutional code rate, interleaving depth, virtual fill length, turbo code rate and turbo information block length.

notes: Superseded by the adoption notice ECSS-E-AS-50-21 (library: ecss-e-as-50-21c-rev-2-5december2024, which adopts CCSDS 131.0-B-5, also in the library as ccsds-131-0-131x0b5). The extraction uses Unicode non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in document IDs, so plain-hyphen regex searches can miss them. Figures (encoder diagrams, ASM bit patterns, randomizer logic) are images; the ASM values are only in Table 8-1 (p. 38). Clause 3.1 cites 'ECSS-ST-00-01' (p. 10) for the normative ECSS-S-ST-00-01, and the note to 6.4.2a cites 'ECSS-E-ST-05' (p. 28) where ECSS-E-ST-50-05 is meant. Superscripts are flattened in the extraction (for example '2 × 106 km' for 2 × 10^6 km, p. 10; 'x8 + x7' for x^8 + x^7). Annex H (p. 68) prints a named licensing contact with postal address, telephone, fax and e-mail; these are deliberately not reproduced here. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; srcgrep shows 70 PDF pages (the last one blank) while the registry gives 69.
